what: 200 tilted (−70°) strips rush in from outside the bottom right of the screen (120vw·50vh) toward the upper left in .5s power2.in in random order (.0015s interval) and cover the screen, the moment all are covered the scene is swapped, then after a .05s pause they leave the same way toward outside the upper left (−120vw·−50vh) in .5s power2.out. Each strip is random: width 2~12vw·height 40~120vh·right −60~10%·top −50~100%, color one of four line colors — the scene transition for game·campaign screens

options.dur: Length in seconds for each cover and uncover, default .5 — shortened in the app
options.each: Start interval between bands (s), default .0015 (random order)
options.hold: Pause before it clears after fully covered (s), default .05
options.ease-in: Cover easing curve, like 0.16,1,0.3,1, default power2.in
options.--fx-line-1~4: Four band colors (via the user’s css) — default --kf-ink · --kf-accent · accent color 45% · --kf-accent-soft
options.[data-fx-part=trigger]: Child that starts the sweep on click. If absent, the sweep is started by sending an fx:sweep event to the element (detail.midway takes the function to call at the fully covered moment) — at the fully covered moment an fx:midway event arrives on the element

use: <body data-fx="stripe-sweep"> … el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("fx:sweep", { detail: { midway: () => changeScene() } }))
note: The numbers that build the bands (count, size, position, start at 120vw/50vh, −70°, four randomized line colors) are exactly the original code. The tween call that covers and clears them sits in an obfuscated part of the original bundle and could not be read — length, curve and spacing are values from the earlier version (hex-arena-racing-game), matched by eye to the original screen.

from.where: shared.js AR.lines — scene transitions for menu↔game and result↔play again
